practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: Class-level @Category(UnitTest.class) is present, providing categorization and enabling selective test execution.
The method contains a single Arrange (new Grafo(1688)), a single Act (grafo0.numVertices()), and a single Assert (assertEquals). Only one method call under test is exercised, so it is atomic.
The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify any shared or static state within the method. No ordering hints or numbered test names indicate inter-test dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path test is present for numVertices. There is no test in the class for error or exceptional flows (e.g., invalid constructor arguments or exception-throwing behavior). The test class contains only one test method, so no error-case coverage is present.
The test uses a single typical value (1688). It does not exercise boundary values such as 0, negative or very large values, nor does it contain names or data indicating boundary testing.

The test method is short and self-contained (< 10 lines of body). There is no duplicated setup across multiple methods (only one method present), so no helper extraction is necessary in this small context.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is short (< 20 lines), has a single linear flow (no loops or conditionals), and adheres to a single Arrange-Act-Assert pattern, indicating low complexity.

The test contains only one assertion (assertEquals) and therefore provides a superficial check. It does not assert multiple properties (e.g., additional sanity checks) that could detect deeper faults.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the visible code. The test is active and runnable (has @Test annotation).
The class-level Javadoc explicitly references requirement REQ-GRAFO-001 for the tested behavior, providing traceability from the test to a requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method uses an explicit timeout parameter (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit performance-related safeguard in this unit test.
The test method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe scenario or expected outcome. Method naming does not follow descriptive patterns like method_condition_expectedResult.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are no explicit auto-generated markers or repetitive auto-generated names (such as test0, test1) in the provided code snippet; no clear sign of heavy automated generation is present.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes Given-When-Then comments and descriptive assertion message, indicating some BDD-style design intent and thoughtful test design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices) and does not access private fields or use reflection, keeping the test focused on observable behavior.
The test uses a specific assertion assertEquals with a descriptive failure message rather than a generic assertTrue, which improves diagnosability.
The method uses succinct Given-When-Then comments and the class has Javadoc describing intent; there is no commented-out code or excessive trivial comments.
The method contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, time-based calls, or Thread.sleep) and uses local setup, so results should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local variables and does not create persistent resources or modify global/static state, so no side-effects are evident.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization for the tests (unit test label) and enabling selective execution.
